title: Declare journeys as topology above interlockings: entrypoint, continuations, explicit terminals

facts.note: Journey artifacts are planner data validated against the canonical journey schema.
Planner authors or edits a journey document.
Task text mentions journey topology or composing routing decisions.
Requires a diff-level observer over journey documents to detect changed continuations/terminals/entrypoints.
Ownership-boundary absorption is a semantic judgement.

fires: Planner adds a new journey that should be startable from Station Master actions.
Planner adds a route to an interlocking used by a journey and must decide whether the route terminates or continues.
Planner wants control to pass to another interlocking after a selected train finishes producing an artifact.
A plan proposes making an interlocking select another interlocking, or making a journey run wagons directly.
doesNotFire: Planner edits only a single interlocking's train selection without touching any journey continuation or terminal.
Planner edits only wagon order inside one linear train.
Work on a Bun JourneyRunner runtime implementation (governed by runtime conventions, not this semantic definition).

given: A journey document composing routing decisions across interlockings, each interlocking selecting exactly one linear train
when: the planner authors or changes the journey's entrypoint, routes, continuations or terminals
then: Declare the journey as {station-entrypoint, entrypoint-interlocking, route-continuations, explicit-terminals}: if exposed, its starting Station Master actions, consumer surfaces and first interlocking; and for every route, after its selected train completes, either an explicit terminal or a continuation from (interlocking_id, route_id) via a named artifact that train produces to the next interlocking.
prefer: Compose interlocking -> train -> interlocking; keep each interlocking a local boundary selecting one linear train.
Ownership: Interlocking selects the train, TrainRunner executes wagons linearly, Journey owns continuation.
Exposed journeys: Bun binds the declared Station Master actions to {journeyId, path} via coder.bun.station-master-journey-routing.
Treat journey artifacts as planner data; a separate Bun runtime may introduce a JourneyRunner.
avoid: Recursive interlockings (one selecting or invoking another).
Moving wagon execution out of TrainRunner, or letting any of the three absorb the others.
Implicitly dangling routes, or continuations not keyed by an artifact the selected train produces.
Encoding runtime execution (e.g. a JourneyRunner) into the semantic journey definition.
why: Keeping continuation in the journey lets routing compose across interlockings without recursive interlockings or split wagon execution, so each boundary stays local and verifiable.
evidence: Exposed journeys list Station Master actions/consumer surfaces and an entrypoint interlocking.
Every (interlocking_id, route_id) reached by the journey has either an explicit terminal or a continuation naming an artifact produced by that route's selected train and a target interlocking.
No interlocking selects another interlocking; wagon execution remains in TrainRunner.
verifier_detail: Journey shape: journey -> {station-entrypoint, entrypoint-interlocking, route-continuations, explicit-terminals}; canonical schema planner-schemas/journey.schema.json.
continuation = binding from one (interlocking_id, route_id) pair, through an artifact produced by that route's selected train, to the next interlocking.
terminal = explicit declaration that a route ends the journey rather than continuing to another interlocking.
station_entrypoint: exposed journeys declare Station Master actions and consumer surfaces; Bun binds those actions to {journeyId, path} via coder.bun.station-master-journey-routing.
audit: schema_version 1.0.0; source kind: family; status: active; introduced_in 0.1.0.
Original name: 'Journey topology — composition above interlockings'.
Term ids: journey (label 'Journey topology'), station_entrypoint, continuation, terminal, ownership_boundary.

splitSuggestion.then: Keep train selection in the interlocking, linear wagon execution in TrainRunner and continuation in the journey; no interlocking recursion and no component absorbs another.

additions.text: The ownership-boundary statement (S007, S010, S021-S022) is an independent obligation; kept as prefer/avoid here and proposed as planner.journey.ownership-boundary.
fires/doesNotFire situations and activation facts were derived from the statement; the source has no explicit activation.
Evidence checks are restatements of source definitions as verifiable conditions.
Coder-facing text exceeds the ~1,000-char guideline because the Bun routing binding (S015) and the planner-data/JourneyRunner clarification (S024) must be reader-facing for lossless placement.
